answer: Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 60 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the oasis ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the kernel review can re-run it. A near-duplicate is rejected at the jade gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
